In [[number theory]], a '''Parshin chain''' is a higher-dimensional analogue of a [[Place (mathematics)|place]] of an [[algebraic number field]]. They were introduced by {{harvtxt|Parshin|1978}} in order to define an analogue of the [[idele class group]] for 2-dimensional [[Scheme (mathematics)|schemes]].

A Parshin chain of dimension ''s'' on a scheme is a finite sequence of [[Glossary of scheme theory#Points|points]] ''p''<sub>0</sub>, ''p''<sub>1</sub>, ..., ''p''<sub>''s''</sub> such that ''p''<sub>''i''</sub> has dimension ''i'' and each point is contained in the closure of the next one.
